heading: Values That Break the Generator
proposed: A table whose first column has no attribute type, such as a reference column placed before any string column, makes UI generation fail with a `NullPointerException` in `getFirstTitleColumnForTable` (`UiTableHelper.java:330`). That helper runs for the bulk delete, bulk remove and bulk call-operation dialogs. Put a string attribute column before any reference column in such a table. An attribute without a data type does not fail: the helper skips it and uses the next string column.

heading: DataFilter (ui:DataFilter)
proposed: Table filter helpers can behave wrongly. In-memory filters (`applyInMemoryFilters`) apply every filter to the original data, so only the last filter takes effect. The single-value filter component throws a `TypeError` when it has a value and no filter list is passed, and its update callback keeps the enumeration values from when it was created. The enumeration operator lookups cast to `keyof typeof _BooleanOperation`; both operation enums define the same four keys, so this is a type-level mistake with no runtime effect today. Workaround: check each filtered result in the generated table and initialise the filter array in a custom hook.

heading: How the Runtime Maps Exceptions to HTTP
proposed: Known issue: a `ClientException` subclass whose `getStatusCode()` returns `null` gets status 400 from the JAX-RS `ClientExceptionMapper`, but the CXF `FaultInterceptor` unboxes the status into an `int` and fails with a `NullPointerException` when the exception reaches the CXF fault path instead of the mapper. Workaround: always return a status code from `getStatusCode()`.

heading: ### Template URI priority and naming helpers
proposed: Non-actor templates get only the default Handlebars context. Values bound to the per-element template context are not passed to them: `JslDslGenerator` calls `evalToContextBuilder` with the model-level evaluation context for non-actor templates (`JslDslGenerator.java:226`), while actor templates receive the per-element context (`:197`). The same pattern appears in the ESM and PSM generators. This is a known defect: check the generated output of such templates and do not rely on a template-context variable inside a non-actor template.

heading: ### RDBMS naming prefixes
proposed: If both ends of a bidirectional many-to-many relation have the same name, the generator emits two junction tables, each with one `C_<NAME>` foreign-key column and no `ID` primary key, so the relation is not stored as one junction table. Give the two relation ends different names. With different names the generator emits one junction table with two foreign-key columns and an `ID` primary key.

heading: ### Spacing and Breakpoints
proposed: Breakpoint keys in a `MuiTab` override must sit inside a slot. The generated Tab fragment puts the `breakpoints.down`, `between` and `up` keys directly under `styleOverrides`, beside `root`. MUI's Tab `overridesResolver` reads only named slots (`root`, `labelIcon`, `iconWrapper`, and similar), so these responsive tab overrides are not applied. Workaround: in an `index.ts.mui-tab.fragment.hbs` override, move each breakpoint block inside `root`.

heading: ## Review Workflow for Incremental Migrations
proposed: Backup table names are not built the same way in every incremental step. The post-check, backup-delete and drop steps truncate the table SQL name to the table name limit minus the backup prefix and underscore, using a plain substring rather than the abbreviation the full path uses. The pre-check step does not truncate. For table names longer than that limit, the pre-check looks for a backup name that the other steps never create. Before running the changelog, check the `BACKUP_` names in the script for long table names.
